How it works — two stages. First, a card in your language may have only the machine draft and no human version yet: First drafts shows those and invites you to write the first one. Once a card has a human version, it moves to Judge, where you compare two versions at a time — far easier than ranking a list — and every choice nudges an Elo score, the way a tournament ranks players. The machine draft is in the pool, so we learn when it's already good enough. Every submission passes a quick quality check (empty text, wrong script, a link, or an untranslated paste is turned away) — but that only stops junk; it never judges your wording. The top-ranked version is not approved — the score only ranks it and moves it up the queue; a native reviewer still reads and vouches it before it ships (§8.11). No account; a name only if you want one; every choice and submission is a public proposal.
